subtitle: Branching on real data, and processing a batch of order rows one at a time.

caption: Python runs the first True branch top to bottom, then skips the rest — else is your catch-all.
continue jumps straight to the next row, skipping whatever comes after it for this one.

eyebrow: while loops — repeating until something changes
code:
attempts = 0
connected = False

while not connected and attempts < 3:
    attempts += 1
    print(f"Attempt {attempts}: trying to connect...")
    if attempts == 3:
        connected = True

print("Connected:", connected, "after", attempts, "attempts")
caption: Forgetting to move toward the exit condition (attempts += 1) is the classic way to write an infinite loop.

code:
order_ids = [1001, 1002, 1004, 1006, 1008]
target = 1004

for order_id in order_ids:
    if order_id == target:
        print("Found it:", order_id)
        break   # no need to keep checking the rest
    print("Checking:", order_id)
caption: Once the target is found, break exits immediately instead of wastefully checking what's left.
